column2: In a greenhouse simulation, YOLO segmentation with ByteTrack recovered 90.1\% of the reference count (count F1 0.898) at 0.2 m/s.
The pipeline produced 9,739 apple landmarks against 9,985 harvested apples (2.46\% undercount); CoTracker3 reached HOTA 42.63\% and IDF1 50.75\%.
YOLOv8m with BoT-SORT counted avocados in orchard video with Absolute Counting Precision 92.68\%, MAE 2.0 and RMSE 3.16.
In 15 citrus videos, BoT-SORT with camera motion compensation and a counting line was used, and grading reached mAP 93.2\%.
On 420 apple trees with two RGB-D cameras at three distances, MAPE was 6.91\% and R2 0.733 (ZED 2, 225 cm).
YOLO v8n-MAFP reached mAP 96.9\%, ALRM-Track reached MOTA 88.2\%, and counting on five greenhouse videos gave MAE 1.4 and 96.6\% mean accuracy.
On strawberry scans, re-identification with MinkPanoptic segmentation reached mean mF1 65.1\%, 9.8 points above the second-best method.
The study localized fruit in 3D across frames on a moving robot with a recursive least-squares estimator.
Fusing two calibrated RGB-D cameras lowered Euclidean localization error by 2.84\%-39.21\% over one camera and reached 6.3 mm 3D accuracy under occlusion.
Mango tracking fused overlap, colour, shape, and diagonal length. The authors reported MOTA of 0.6513 and relative count error of 4.30\%.
The dataset has 3,992 images of 953 trees with 9,823 unique bunches; YOLO26m AP50 was 53.1\% and SVR counting Class $\pm$1 75.35\%.
Projecting segmented cotton bolls into a reconstructed plot gave count MAPE of 5.43\% with Lumix imagery on low-density, post-defoliation plots.
The system counted 1,963 pears against 1,891 reference fruits (3.8\% error) with density MAE 0.64 fruit/m2; 53 double counts remained.
YOLO-MSRF segmented tomatoes in RGB-NIR (mAP50 97.8\%), and DeepSORT with trajectory linking gave mean counting accuracy above 90\%.
YOLOv8 with StrongSORT counted tomatoes per ripeness stage in greenhouse sequences against per-class reference counts; ripeness classification accuracy peaked at 81\%.
From UAV apple point clouds, regression against per-section counts gave R2 of about 0.99, and DBSCAN was used for locations.
For strawberry, BoT-SORT with GNSS RTK was used across nine size-maturity categories, with length MAE of 2.51 mm.
Fruits are oriented 3D boxes in an incrementally updated global frame, with 3D GIoU association suppressing duplicates; no numbers are given.
For UAV grape video, SORT+ raised counting accuracy from 33\% to 96\% and cut ID switches by 62\% without re-ID training data.
On seven MOrangeT sequences, HOTA was 47.46\% and the count 978 against 879 annotated fruits (11.26\% error), not exceeding earlier work.
The study used single-tree citrus, 360-degree rotation video and DeepSORT.
BoT-SORT reached HOTA 62.4\% and MOTA 68.4\%; region-based counting reached 92.8\% mean accuracy, 8.8 and 29.9 points above line and ID-accumulation methods.
Semantic NeRF with adaptive clustering raised counting accuracy by 9.0 percentage points over a 3D baseline.
Grounded-SAM2 in flight mode A reached MOTSA 34.84\% and sMOTSA 14.95\%; 2,729 apples in one row were reconstructed (diameter RMSE 1.85 cm).
ByteTrack-DIoU raised MOTA by 5.5, 5.7 and 4.3 points over SORT, DeepSORT and BoT-SORT; tracking-based counting accuracy averaged 88.4\%.
For grapes, multi-view tracks with epipolar constraints and no appearance descriptors reached F1 of 78.7--88.5\% on 30 bunches.
For cherry tomatoes with a robot, multi-view compensation reduced counting error by 95.6\%, and counting accuracy was 95.2\%.
For grapes, semantic ORB-SLAM3 with DBSCAN was applied in dynamic environments.
NeRF from posed multi-view images fitted berries as RANSAC spheres; count MAE was 0.50 berries (10 bunches), segmentation AP 92.1\% (52 bunches).
For grapes across days, branch-based 3D alignment (SfM and SIFT) with spatial proximity association was used.
Hough voting in 3D Gaussian space was tested on apple, sweet pepper and synthetic data, with the largest gains under dense occlusion.
NeRF tuned with 2D masks was applied to synthetic fruit and soybean for 3D segmentation, not primarily counting.
An improved YOLOv5s reached mAP50 of 99.2\%; DeepSORT counting gave 86.82\% mean accuracy with R2 0.9677 on ten videos.
Coconuts at three maturity stages were tracked with Kalman-Hungarian association.
Tracked grape bunches were 27-74\% of annotations with multi-view acquisition and 13-23\% with single view; bunch-size R2 rose from 0.39 to 0.53.
On five videos, YOLOv7-Tiny-PDE+DeepSort reached MOTA 91.3\%, IDF1 91\% and IDSW 5.7 (baseline 89.3\%, 82\%, 12.3); detection mAP50 was 97.90\%.
On RGB-D apple fruitlet video, boxes in stable-count frames were linked with the Hungarian algorithm; mean count error was 0.63 fruitlets.
A 1D-ConvNet with SAM2 on hyperspectral images raised recall by 25 percent over RGB YOLOv8s, with detections localized in unified 3D coordinates.
For camellia, ByteTrack was combined with a regression from surface fruit to total fruit.
A UAV in a controlled environment used LiDAR mapping to avoid recounting, reaching 98\% accuracy in simulation and 90\% in real tests.
Predicted counts were 303 of 358 oranges (84.6\%) in Video 1 and 441 of 589 (74.8\%) in Video 2.
Apple counts per block from UAV photogrammetric point clouds reached R2 of about 0.41 (7.5 m) and 0.40 and 0.53 (10 m).
For persimmon, 3D Gaussian Splatting reached 96\% counting accuracy, 16\% above NeRF methods.
For mandarin oranges in 360-degree video, a transformer fused features across angles to regress the count.
For 20 common fruit classes, ByteTrack reached 75.33\% accuracy against manual counts.
For cotton, plot-level NeRF with a modified FruitNeRF was tested with two acquisition modes.
For grapes, YOLOv12 with BoT-SORT performed best, with 84.31\% relative counting accuracy.
Apples were counted from UAV orthophotos, with an experimental correction coefficient for hidden fruit planned.
For multi-session 4D apple mapping, position, visual and topology association gave 96.9\% counting accuracy (1,790 apples, 60 trees).
For greenhouse melons with an AGV, a counting line gave 2.74\% count error with front-row annotation.
For lychee, a gated association metric based on distance intersection over union and an area-based counting strategy were used.
Mean counting accuracy was 80.0\%; HOTA, MOTA and IDF1 rose by 4.3, 2.2 and 2.5 points, and YOLOv9s parameters fell 29.6\%.
Dual-association tracking reached HOTA 58.6\%, MOTA 64.7\% and IDF1 80.0\%; mean counting precision was 93.1\% with MAE 1.3\%.
For common fruits, DeepSORT with an ROI line was used.
A stereo-camera system for detecting, tracking and counting apples, robust to intermittent occlusion, gave orchard counts with errors of 15\% to 57\%.
On infrared greenhouse video, the tracker counted 67 of 70 peppers (MOTA 85\%); the RGB stream counted 25 of 70 (MOTA 34\%).
On six synthetic fruit types, mean counting F1 was 0.925 with ground-truth masks and 0.776 with Detic masks; real apples gave 0.765.
Summarizing per-frame regression estimates over video segments lowered MedAE from 2.79-3.20 (1 frame) to 2.31-2.51 (11 frames).
YOLOv8s with ByteTrack and a counting ROI on 20 greenhouse videos gave R2 0.914, MAE 8.55 fruits and MAPE 9.52\%.
A YOLO camera on a trolley tracked tomatoes across frames to avoid double counting; yield prediction differed from harvest by 6.85\%.
A modified MangoYOLO5 with improved centroid tracking reached mAP 93.6\%, and the reported counts were close to the manually labelled ground truth.
For drone-imaged calamansi, ByteTrack performed best (MOTA 59.67\%, HOTA 65.42\%, IDF1 73.72\%) against SORT and DeepSORT.
For truss tomatoes, SORT, DeepSORT, ByteTrack and BoT-SORT were compared across frame rates, using a public MOT dataset of 165,172 instances.
For pergola grapes in smartphone video, ByteTrack gave counts 27\% above the true value.
Per-stage counts from row panoramas correlated with farmer counts at r 0.96 (1-40\%) and 0.63 (41-80\%); weekly yield WAPE was 21.35\%.
Counting ripe strawberries with a counting line on greenhouse UAV video gave 45 of 47, 46 of 49 and 44 of 49.
AppleYOLO combines an improved YOLOv8 with Deep OC-SORT to count apples without double counting, reaching mAP50 98.5\% and mAP50-95 79.8\%.
For greenhouse cherry tomatoes, instance segmentation with SfM/MVS and Nerfacto from daily video gave a mean size error of 8.01\% against calipers.
YOLOv8n reached mAP50 86.3\% at 6.2 MB; OC-SORT reached HOTA 67.10\%, above BoT-SORT, ByteTrack and StrongSORT, with central region counting.
For ripe and unripe oranges, DeepSORT reached 92.3\% counting precision.
A 3D semantic reconstruction with ORB-SLAM3 on an unmanned vehicle gave relative errors of 14.36\% for tomato count and 14.25\% for volume.
Region tracking-counting (ByteTrack with a region derived by particle swarm optimization) reached a mean counting error of 6.6\% on 9 videos, versus 11.6\% for ByteTrack and 8.7\% for a line.
For apples with stereo, GPS and visual odometry, OC-SORT performed best (HOTA 59\%), with RMSE 6.24\% and R2 0.96.
STF-YOLO reached mAP50 79.7\%; with ByteTrack, mean counting accuracy on three videos was 72.49\%, versus 72.08\% for OC-SORT and 40.31\% for StrongSORT.
On 10 pineapple drone videos, PineSORT reached MOTA 72.3\%, HOTA 66.9\%, IDF1 85.8\% and 218 IDSW; BoTSORT reached IDF1 81.1\%, 795 IDSW.
For greenhouse tomatoes with a depth-camera robot, DeepSORT per ripeness stage reached MOTA 82.35\%.
APYOLO reached mAP50 of 82.0\%; DeepSORT with unique identities and a line-crossing rule on 10 apple-tree videos gave about 84.45\% counting accuracy.
For vertical hydroponics, a semantic-metric SLAM based on a 3D scene graph with a sensor uncertainty model was used.
In one example, low-altitude video near a small citrus tree with 12 fruits recovered all 12; no other count error was reported.
A dynamic Kalman tracker with IoU association and Re-ID reached MOTA 95.0\% and HOTA 82.4\% on apple video; counting gave R2 0.85.
For blueberry, ByteTrack with trajectory completion reduced double counting caused by missed detections.
A two-container verification rule raised kiwifruit count accuracy from 40.12\% to 94.20\% for ByteTrack and from 37.59\% to 96.65\% for DeepSORT.
Tomato truss tracking MOTA was 95.4-98.0\% (YOLOv8 with DeepSORT 52.4-60.0\%) and mean truss counting accuracy was 97.30\%.
YOLO-Banana with DeepSORT on RGB-D video counted banana bunches with 96.82\% mean per-row accuracy (6 rows, 61 bunches).
For grapes, SiamFC was used to identify unique bunches per panel, with weights from an empirical calibration distribution.
Across 44 strawberry videos, the two-region count had $R^2=0.91$ against manual counts, compared with 0.68 for counting track identifiers.
The dataset has 11 UAV vineyard videos with 5,958 MOTS-annotated frames; bunch IDs persist across frames and perspectives. No counting result.
For common fruits, DeepSORT was combined with ARIMA forecasting.
CottonSense tracked cotton on 16 field videos and counted four stages; R2 against hand counts was 0.88-0.97 (mean 0.93).
DeepSort with added appearance matching reached an average counting precision of 95.33\% versus 88.13\% for original DeepSort; identity switches fell from 68 to 48.
On 10 citrus videos, DeepSORT with a two-stage life filter cut ID switch rate from 25.97\% to 15.63\%; counting precision was 81.02\%.
For apples, OCSort reached HOTA 60.24\%, and linear regression reduced prediction error, in a ROS simulator.
A tracker with LoFTR-based spatial association outperformed comparison methods on LettuceMOT by up to 25\% on average.
For greenhouse eggplant, motion parallax was used to prevent double counting per bed.
For tomato, ByteTrack performed best against Motpy and FairMOT, with R2 0.93 and RMSE 9.17.
A histogram filter on three monocular poses gave tomato 3D position MAE below 10 mm in simulation, about 20 mm in laboratory.
On four datasets, filtered absolute percentage count errors were 12.88\%, 4.56\%, 0.84\% and 1.06\% (MOTA 61-94\%); ByteTrack had 4.26-113.94\%.
Apples in merged UAV frames were detected with a modified YOLOv5; only detection was evaluated (precision 92.1\% sunny, 90.8\% cloudy, 82.7\% shade).
FruitNeRF uses a semantic field from posed images plus clustering, tested on real apples and six synthetic fruits.
On TexCot22, NTrack reached IDF1 92.49\%, HOTA 73.56\% and MOTA 89.25\%; boll count MAPE was 4.00\%, versus 15\% (ByteTrack) and 55\% (DeepSORT).
YOLOv7 with eight side frames counted 133 fruits against 130 manual on one tree (97.7\% accuracy) and 95.48\% accuracy on 14 trees.
For tomatoes at three ripeness levels, RGB and multispectral imaging gave per-class counts per group.
The tracker assigned each tomato cluster its most frequent maturity level. Reported count accuracy was 92.79\%, and maturity accuracy excluding counting errors was 90.84\%.
A neural-network regressor using video counts and tree data reached R2 0.85 against manual counts with at least 30\% of fruits counted.
On four table-grape sequences, AgriSORT reached MOTA 65.93/66.13/62.21/45.08 and led on both CloseUp sequences, while SORT was better on Overview2.
The platform mapped pear crop load and blush coverage. Calibrated crop-load errors across two years were 4.0--6.4\% in 3D canopies and below 2.5\% in multileader vertical trellises.
YOLOv7 with a multi-head attention mechanism and ByteTrack counted 1,691 apples against 1,645 manual (MAPE 0.027), whereas DeepSORT counted 1,970 (MAPE 0.197).
YOLOv5s-little (mAP 99.5\%) with an improved DeepSORT reached HOTA 79.6\%, MOTA 92.58\% and IDF1 95.02\%; mean counting accuracy was 95.1\%.
One camera perpendicular to the canopy detected up to 88.3\% of the fruits detected by four cameras; two cameras up to 97.5\%.
YOLOv5 with DeepSORT reached MOTA 88\% and 0.87 on two simulated videos; the abstract states 85.7\% counting accuracy without a count table.
COF-YOLO v8n reached P 97.7\%, R 97\% and mAP 99\%; dynamic counting fed detector output to DeepSORT. No counting error is given.
Multi-view estimation of dragon fruit gave position RMSE of 7 cm and radius RMSE of 7 mm. MAPE for the weight of individual fruit was about 16\%.
KiwiDetector (YOLOv7) reached mAP50 93.7\%; KiwiTracker reached average counting precision 80.2\% on 10 videos, with model counts always larger.
In situ 3D reconstruction of cotton from oblique UAV images counted bolls with R2 0.92, better than nadir images (R2 0.73).
AD-YOLO with MR-SORT on 7 apple videos counted 8,984 fruits against 8,447 ground truth, with MOTA 85.6\% and R2 0.98.
On five strawberry plants, counts from the semantic point cloud map differed from true counts by 10.87\% on average; mIoU was 73.2\%.
For nectarines with a robot dog, camera motion compensation raised MOTA by 2.9\% (MOTA 63.4\%).
Citrus detection with illumination adjustment and DeepSORT gave count MAPE of 4.36\% offline and 12.66\% in online UAV operation.
For ripe and unripe strawberries, MultiMap gave occlusion robustness, with relative count error 6.7\% overall and 8.7\% and 9.9\% per class.
For citrus, NeRF rays with DBSCAN were used for deduplication, giving MAE 1.5 fruits per tree.
For citrus, 2, 4 or 6 views and pruning intensity were studied with XGBoost; the optimal number of views depends on pruning.
Deep SORT with a vertical ROI line reached maximum counting accuracy of 86.6\% (YOLOv5, YOLOv7) on 30 apples on an artificial tree.
The dataset has 40 UAV RGB videos of four vineyard rows; 29 are MOTS-annotated with consistent bunch identities. No counting result.
For white grapes from UAVs, PointTrack MOTS was used with a public dataset.
For table grapes, EKF multi-object tracking with robot motion and RGB-D was tested in simulator and laboratory.
On a video with 31 grape bunches, the SfM tracker reached MOTA 55.756 and 9\% count error; DeepSORT reached 50.624 and 26\%.
For loose oil-palm fruits, trees were tracked across frames and the per-tree count was the most frequent count over n frames.
For apples, ByteTrack (HOTA 68.9\%) was compared with SORT and DeepSORT; MAPE was 7.47\% one week before harvest.
YOLOv4 with centroid tracking and the Dlib tracker counted 204 green oranges of 208 visible; without the tracker, 215 (25 double counts).
YOLO v7 with Soft-NMS reached detection F1 90.09\%; DeepSort reached 89.87\% mean tracking accuracy, and ID-based counting accuracy was 97.49\%.
On three apple videos (290 fruits manually), YOLOv7-CA with cascade SURF matching counted 310; SORT counted 373, and YOLOv7 without tracking 495.
The Simplified network reached mAP50 of 82.4\% and counted 235 strawberries, 1,562 jujubes and 7,359 cherries; counts were compared only across networks.
For blueberry, three views (top, left, right) from a multi-camera platform were used, with regression to correct overlap between views.
In UAV video of longan, DeepSORT tracked fruits and the maximum ID was the count; mean error was 2.66\% (clusters), 2.99\% (fruits).
An improved YOLOv5s reached AP 95.26\% (up 3.51 points); with DeepSort, mean MOTA over ten videos rose from 88.95\% to 90.83\%.
YOLOv5s with ByteTrack using camera motion compensation and line counting reached MOTA 64.6\% and 82.8\% mean counting accuracy on bagged grape video.
On 10 branches, two-sided scanning reached 81.17\% counting accuracy versus 73.7\% for one-sided scanning.
Best count error (MAPE) was 5.06\% and highest tracking HOTA 71.47\% for tomatoes on seven plants, each recorded from 100 successive viewpoints.
A pruned YOLOv5s detector, SORT, and counting lines gave mean grape-cluster count accuracy of 84.9\% against manual counts on eight videos.
For oil-palm fresh fruit bunches moving on a conveyor, a detector with frame-to-frame centroid tracking reached counting accuracy of up to 100\%.
For citrus per tree, UAV images with ground counts gave MAPE 23.45\% from one side versus 25.72\% from two sides.
With perfect detection, MHT reached MOT accuracy 97.00\% and DeepSORT 93.00\%; with deep detectors, DeepSORT had the lowest count errors (20.07\%, 31.52\%).
For apples, reciprocal and secondary matching gave ID switch 3.9\% and MOTA 89.9\%.
For a multi-arm harvesting robot, multi-camera extrinsic calibration with fruit-surface point cloud matching removed repeated detections.
For sweet pepper, graph-based viewpoint planning was used to cover fruits.

For citrus from multiple UAVs, DeepSORT with a non-uniform distributed counter reached F1 89.07\% and MAPE 12.75\% on 19 trees under suitable light, and MAPE 15.59--15.99\% under weak or strong light.
For strawberries in overlapping images from a camera towed above the beds, FaceNet with position and clustering identified unique objects, outperforming orthomosaics.
For strawberries in smartphone video, StrongSORT with DynCount reached 92.05\% counting accuracy.
Counting accuracy exceeded 84\% for tomato trusses and 86\% for single fruits in greenhouse experiments with an inspection robot.
For loose oil-palm fruits under trees, trees were tracked across frames and the per-tree count was the mode of per-frame counts.
Tomatoes and flowers were counted from drone video with YOLOv5 and DeepSORT; counting accuracy was 85\% (red), 99\% (green) and 50\% (flowers).
Tracking the apple trunk supplied a motion reference for consecutive frames. Fruit counts had reported accuracy of 91.49\% against manual video counts.
A lightweight YOLOv5s reached mAP 97.9\% for red tomatoes; DeepSORT counting was demonstrated only on tomato flowers, without count error.
Cascade matching recovered 310 apples against 292 across three videos and 44 \textit{Camellia} fruit against 38 in one video.
In three simulated scenarios, superellipsoid matching found more fruits than the earlier octree approach; real greenhouse data were qualitative only.
Terrestrial laser scans merged into a colored point cloud were clustered with optimized mean shift, giving a mean detection rate of 81.73\%.
On tomato row panoramas, detected fruit count differed from annotation by 2.32\%, with precision 82.12\%, recall 84.08\% and F1 83.09\%.
For apples from UAVs, FlowNet2 optical flow with Hungarian matching reached 90.39\% yield accuracy.
After removing duplicate fruits, counts reached R2 0.9737 (apple) and 0.9562 (orange) with RMSE 10.0920 and 4.2544.
OrangeYolo reached mAP 95.7\%; counting with OrangeSort on six sequences gave MAE 0.081, better than Sort (0.45) and DeepSort (1.212).
KinectV2 images from two viewpoints were registered into one point cloud per tomato plant; PointRCNN detected fruits with precision 86.19\%, recall 83.39\%.
Front and back tree counts were summed and multiplied by an orchard correction factor; count errors were 4.3\%, 4.93\% and 4.25\%.
On 9 potted kumquat plants (149 fruits), recall was 85.91\%, precision 79.01\%, F1 82.32\%; R2 of predicted versus true count was 0.97.
For unstripped oil-palm bunches in a mill, Faster R-CNN with frame-to-frame centroid tracking was used and counts were evaluated.

On nine orchards, mean percentage error against packhouse counts was 26\% (farm estimate from about 5\% of trees), 13\% (hand count of 18 calibration trees), 11\% (raw multi-view count) and 17\% (multi-view count corrected with the calibration trees).
On 10 orchard videos, YOLOv4-tiny tracking gave mean counting precision 81.94\% and R2 0.986 against manual counts.
For apples, tree trunk tracking was used with a vertical fruit wall.
For pear and apple in walking video, a Kalman filter counted 226 of 234 pears.
A multi-class fruit tracking system with re-identification reached MAPE 3\%, whereas a baseline multi-object tracker had MAPE 21\%.
MangoYOLO counts from two-sided images, corrected for hidden fruit, reached R2 0.98 against harvest counts; the model did not hold across seasons.
YOLOv3 and DeepSORT with ResNet18 features counted apples in three full-row videos with 90.6\%, 93.0\% and 95.8\% accuracy.
For apples, DeepSORT with ResNet features was used.
YOLOv4-512 with Deep SORT: the unique-ID method reached count F1 87.85\% and MOTA 75.47\%, versus 72.94\% and 56.60\% for the ROI line.
After rootstock-specific calibration, the mobile platform gave RMSE of 5 fruits per tree on apples and orchard-level error below 5\%.
For hydroponic tomato with a robot, Faster R-CNN with a hue ripeness standard and centroid-tracking counts reached 88.6\% detection accuracy (53 fruits).
The projected area of points classified as grape correlated with harvest weight: R2 0.81 (Gr-19), 0.56 (Gr-20) and 0.63 (Ga-20).
In simulation Scenario 2 (28 fruits), the utility approach found 27.0 $\pm$ 2.4 fruits; the real greenhouse test had no numerical analysis.
Apples were detected by colour in SfM point clouds with recall 74.50-90.62\% and precision 48.64-66.66\%; assignment to parent trees exceeded 95\% accuracy.
Faster R-CNN counted apples on per-tree orthomosaic crops with precision above 90\%; image counts regressed on harvested fruit gave R2 0.80.
Apple counts from merged two-sided reconstructions reached 91.98\%-94.81\% of harvest counts, whereas summing per-side counts gave 101.93\%-150\%.
For apples, multi-view LiDAR and forced airflow each added 6.5\% and 6.7\% more localized fruits; yield RMSE was below 6\%.
On 11 apple trees with 1,455 fruits, Mask R-CNN with SfM and SVM raised F1 from 0.816 (2D) to 0.881 (3D).
Fuji-SfM comprises 582 sequential images, 3D models of 11 trees and 1,455 apples with 3D locations.
LFuji-air provides LiDAR point clouds of 11 apple trees with 8 scans per tree, multi-view and with airflow.

Merged two-side row counts reached 95.56\%-97.83\% of harvested apples with the ResNet50 detector and 91.98\%-94.81\% with the GMM detector; summing per-side counts gave 103.86\%-147.81\% and 101.93\%-150\%, respectively.
Stitching kiwi canopy images with SURF, RANSAC and homography gave yield estimates 15\% and 6\% above post-harvest weights on two orchards.
Mask R-CNN reached instance segmentation F1 up to 0.91 on 408 grape bunches; SfM-based 3D association was shown only qualitatively.
For lemons on a harvester, Kuhn-Munkres matching agreed over 95\% with visual counts.
For cotton, SfM from multi-view images with density clustering reached up to 90\% boll counting accuracy.
Aligning two-sided LiDAR point clouds with ICP gave fruit counts of 85.4-94.8\% of manual counts in foliated trees, with best F1 89.5.
Sweet pepper point clouds fused from multiple RGB-D views were counted with subtractive clustering, giving TPR 90.69\% and FPR 6.97\%.
Mango counts from two-sided hyperspectral images were optimized against field and RGB counts; test R2 was 0.75 (18 trees), 0.83 (216 trees).
For multiple fruit types in greenhouses, feature matching, optical flow and projective transformation were combined.
On 18 mango trees, the monocular system had mean count error 27.8 and R2 0.78; the LiDAR comparison had 19.8 and 0.88.
Counts from registered LiDAR point clouds against harvest counts gave R2 0.63 on 12 pruned citrus trees, not significant on 12 unpruned.
For grapes, object-level stereo SLAM reached F1 0.977 against image counts.
One-sided counting with homography tracking reached 89\%-98\% of visible apples; merged two-sided counts reached 91.98\%-94.81\% accuracy, versus 101.93\%-150\% for direct summing.
On a row of 21 trees with 3,286 harvested fruits, video tracking counted 2,050 (62.3\%) versus 1,322 (40.2\%) from two-view images.
Sequential night images were stitched so canopy segments recorded twice were analysed once; berry detection had recall 0.8764 and precision 0.9582.
Two-sided row 3D reconstructions were merged and detections projected to 3D and clustered to avoid double counting; yield accuracy was 96-97\%.
For oranges and apples, FCN with KLT, Kalman and Hungarian tracking was followed by SfM to reject duplicate tracks and outliers.
For apples, active viewpoint planning for counting apples in clusters used a combinatorial world model.
Apples in clusters were counted with a Gaussian mixture; counting algorithm accuracy was 91\%, and 81-85\% when combined with segmentation and registration.
For apples in a two-sided tunnel, 3D location removed duplicates; accuracy was 82\% (two sides) versus 58\% (one side).
For apples with a single camera, incremental piece-by-piece SfM was used for registration and counting.
On 16 mango trees, multi-view counts against harvest counts gave slope 1.014 with R2 0.90; single view counted only 27\% of fruits.
Counts from six images per tree were calibrated to yield; validation tree estimation error was -10.49\% to 9.37\% (Approach 1).
Mean absolute error in recognizing apples seen twice from both canopy sides was 12\% with a buffer distance of one apple diameter.
For grapes over four seasons, registered images from a vehicle with image-size-to-yield calibration explained up to 75\% of spatial variance.
For grapes, visual counts were modelled and calibrated to yield, with 3-4\% error given calibration data.
For sweet pepper in a greenhouse with over 28,000 images, statistical aggregation of repeated observations gave a correlation of 74.2\% without adjustment.
Linear regression on fruit-patch counts from both sides of 40 Fuji apple trees performed best, with R2 0.81 and NRMSE 0.43.
For apples, night stereo from an autonomous vehicle with sequential image registration gave errors of -3.2\% and 1.2\% per block.
For oil-palm bunches, 809 bunches were tagged and monitored from anthesis to harvest (about 30,000 images), recording age and harvest date.
In simulated UAV missions, tomato, pepper, and eggplant fruit were counted from both sides of each bed and merged by position; the mean fruit-count score was 49.88 of 50 over 500 missions.
Watermelons in field video were detected by YOLOv8 and tracked with SORT, counted when a box centre crossed a line; the example frame showed 9, with no reference count.
Citrus in UAV video was detected with an improved YOLOv8n and linked across frames by DeepSORT; counting accuracy against the mean of three manual counts was 95.57\% on 10 videos.
Cherry tomatoes in greenhouse robot video were linked by ByteTrack and binned by maturity; total counting accuracy against manual labels was 90.2\% in greenhouse S1 and 87.1\% in S2.
Blueberry plants were imaged from two sides without linking berries; the best strategy averaged two per-side yield estimates from single-side ripe counts, giving R2 of 0.80 for plant yield.
Cherry tomatoes in stitched dual-camera greenhouse video were tracked with an improved DeepSORT; counts of three ripeness classes against ground truth gave RMSE 3.11 and R2 0.998.
Apples in UAV multi-view images were reconstructed by structure from motion and counted as 3D instances; against manual counts, R2 was 0.84 to 0.99 and WMAPE 3.41\% to 12.75\%.
Tomato clusters in greenhouse robot video were detected from RGB-D input, tracked with ByteTrack, and counted in a tracking region; mean accuracy was 95.1\% against 529 manual counts.
Apples in tree-row video were given IDs by trunk tracking after thresholds removed back-row and ground detections; counting accuracy was 95.0\% and R2 0.97 on 10 videos.
Mango and almond fruits were tracked across frames and placed in a 3D map by monocular depth and visual odometry; on 18 mango trees the mean absolute error was 33.80\%.
Green citrus was counted from walk-around video with YOLOv5-CS and DeepSORT, counting at a virtual region; average relative error was 8.75\% on real trees and 4.25\% on simulated trees.
Kiwifruit in under-canopy UAV video was detected with YOLOv7 and counted by SORT through a region of interest; the real-time half-row count was 84.3\% of the harvest-based reference.

Grapevine berries in three vertically overlapping images were deduplicated by matching bunch patches; per-plant counts in vertical shoot positioned vines had a mean absolute error of 45 berries (6.9\%).
Holly fruits on one tree were imaged by a circling UAV, stitched into a SIFT panorama, counted with YOLOX; statistical rate against actual count exceeded 96\% within 1.2 m radius.
Apples imaged from both tree-row sides were reconstructed as SfM-MVS point clouds and multi-detections merged manually; no count was reported, and diameter MAE was 3.7 mm (R2 0.91).

Fuji apples on six trees were reconstructed as SfM-MVS point clouds, with image detections projected into 3D and multi-detections merged manually, giving 615 annotated apples; no counting result was reported.
Apples were matched between monthly stereo sessions by SIFT features and camera pose; 74\% of fully visible fruit detected in September were matched in October.
Cherry tomato clusters in plant-row videos were linked by a multi-frame tracker; predicted totals were 159, 76, and 86 clusters against manual counts of 164, 78, and 86.

Oranges were detected with Faster R-CNN in UAV images from both sides of 20 trees, without described cross-view linking; a long short-term memory network gave per-tree yield with a standard error of 4.53\% against harvest weights.
Cherry tomatoes in video were given unique identities by DeepSORT to avoid double counting; DeepSORT scored better than SORT on tracking metrics, and no count error was reported.
Coffee branch images were reconstructed by SfM and points classified by ripeness, so ripeness percentage came from classified point counts, not fruit counts, with errors of 3.7\% to 8.7\%.
Red apples imaged at night from both row sides were triangulated by stereo and merged within 0.16 m; the mean count error per row was $-2.9$\% in thinned rows and $-41.3$\% in unthinned rows.
The authors reported mean tracking efficiency of 93.4\% at sampled frames of apple video with YOLOv11 and ByteTrack. This was a track-retention measure.
Stereo positions and overlapping 3D boxes linked \textit{Camellia oleifera} detections. Counts over four trees were 0.47--4.19\% below the reported reference totals.
Olive counts from opposite sides used scale factors of 3.18 in sun and 2.20 under cloud, derived from hand counts in images of five trees and estimated harvest totals.
Predicting the position of swinging citrus reduced mean grasping time by 5.6 s to 12.8 s in the potted-tree experiment.
Front and rear images were combined for 60 simulated pepper beds. The authors reported correct counts for 86.67\% of the tested image pairs.
Fusing point clouds from several views of sweet peppers gave mean relative errors of 1.72\% in width and 1.60\% in height against manual measurements.
With detection and tracking held fixed on greenhouse video, the best tested relative-depth filter increased the reported count accuracy from 81.17\% to 93.80\%.
On 50 paired apple frames, median position errors were 5.73 mm from the near camera, 8.25 mm from the far camera, and 6.43 mm from their weighted combination.
Cultivar-specific calibration of two opposing mango images gave a relative RMSE of 14\% on 52 validation trees. Pixel F1 fell from 0.73 in uniform material to 0.48 across heterogeneous orchards.
On 18 mango calibration trees, RMSE against harvest was 25 fruit/tree for masked dual views and 15 for masked multi-view counts.
Orchard factors fitted to summed opposing mango views ranged from 1.05 to 2.43 over five orchards. Estimates differed from packhouse totals by 4.6--15.2\%.
Calibrated apple yield totals were usually within 10\% of the reference. Single-tree error dispersion remained above 25\% of the mean yield.

On 10 citrus trees filmed with a handheld smartphone, FairMOT with a lightweight backbone and Byte association reached a mean count accuracy of 91.61\% (R2 0.9858, RMSE 4.17 fruit) against counts verified manually in the video.
